cards.text: The LORD is still speaking to Moses, Israel's leader, and now He's handing out the calendar. He tells Moses to say to the Israelites, “These are My appointed feasts, the feasts of the LORD that you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies.” Friend, this might be the first schedule in history that people actually look FORWARD to.

cards.question: First on God's list is the one that comes every week: the Sabbath, on the seventh day. True or false: On the Sabbath, Israel can do a little work as long as they're at home.

cards.text: Now come the yearly feasts, and first up is the Passover to the LORD, beginning at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. God gives an EXACT time, friend, and back in the drawer we told time by how much dust had piled up on us.

cards.question: On the fifteenth day of that same month, a seven-day feast begins. What kind of bread does God say Israel must eat all seven days?
True or false: The Feast of Unleavened Bread has a sacred assembly on its first day and another on its seventh day, with no regular work on either one.

cards.text: Then the LORD gives Moses another message, this one for a day that's still coming. When Israel enters the land He's giving them and reaps its harvest, they bring the priest a sheaf of the firstfruits of that harvest.

cards.question: The priest takes that first sheaf of the harvest. What does he do with it before the LORD?

cards.text: That same day, a year-old lamb without blemish goes up as a burnt offering, with fine flour mixed with oil and a drink offering of wine, and God calls it a pleasing aroma. In the Millers' kitchen, a pleasing aroma meant people I didn't even know LIVED there came walking up to the counter.

cards.question: True or false: Once the harvest comes in, Israel can start eating the new grain before that first sheaf has been brought to God.

cards.text: Then God starts a countdown. From the day the sheaf is waved, Israel counts off seven full weeks, which is the longest I've ever waited for anything except getting out of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Seven full weeks, right up to the day after the seventh Sabbath. In all, Israel counts off ___ days and then brings the LORD an offering of new grain.
From their homes, Israel brings two loaves of bread as firstfruits to the LORD. How are those two loaves baked?

cards.text: Along with that bread comes a big lineup of offerings: seven lambs, a young bull, two rams, a goat and two more lambs. The priest waves the bread and the two lambs before the LORD, and they're holy to the LORD for the priest.

cards.question: On the day of new grain, Israel holds a sacred assembly with no regular work. How long does God say Israel is to keep this day?

cards.text: Then, right in the middle of the feasts, God gives a harvest rule: don't reap all the way to the edges of the field, and don't gather the gleanings. Friend, I've watched bakers fight over the LAST crumb on the tray, so this is a big ask.

cards.question: God tells Israel to leave the edges of the field and the gleanings of the harvest. Who are they left for?

answers.text: The poor and the foreign resident

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses again, and the calendar jumps to the seventh month. On the first day of that month, Israel gets a day of rest and a sacred assembly, announced by something LOUD.

cards.question: What announces the day of rest and sacred assembly on the first day of the seventh month?

cards.text: Trumpet blasts, friend, and somewhere my Mags, the bell, is SO jealous right now. Then on the tenth day of that same month comes the Day of Atonement.

cards.question: On the Day of Atonement, Israel holds a sacred assembly and presents a food offering to the LORD. What else does God tell them to do?
True or false: On the Day of Atonement, a little regular work is fine once the sacred assembly is over.

cards.text: No work, because it's the Day of Atonement, when atonement is made for them before the LORD their God. And God is serious: anyone who doesn't humble himself must be cut off from his people, and anyone who does any work on this day, God says He will destroy.

cards.question: God calls the Day of Atonement a Sabbath of complete rest. When does that Sabbath begin?

answers.text: The evening of the ninth day

cards.text: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the Feast of Tabernacles to the LORD begins, and it runs seven days. That's feast number... hold on, I spent YEARS counting dust and I still lost count.

cards.question: True or false: When the seven days of the Feast of Tabernacles are done, there's still an eighth day, and it's a solemn assembly.

cards.text: Then God wraps up the list: these are His appointed feasts, each with its own offerings on its own designated day. And all of that comes on top of the Sabbath offerings, the gifts, the vows and the freewill offerings.
But God circles back to the Feast of Tabernacles for a little more. It comes after Israel has gathered the produce of the land, with complete rest on the first day and on the eighth.

cards.question: On the first day of the Feast of Tabernacles, God tells Israel to gather something. What is it?
The harvest is in and the branches are gathered. Then God tells Israel to ___ before the LORD their God for seven days.

cards.text: Then comes the camping part. For seven days, all the native-born of Israel must dwell in booths, and friend, after years in a junk drawer, a booth sounds like a BEACH HOUSE to me.

cards.question: God brought Israel out of Egypt. Why does He want them living in booths for seven days every year?

answers.text: So their descendants know God made Israel dwell in booths
So they can stay close to their fields at harvest
So their houses are free for travelers that week

cards.question: True or false: Moses keeps the appointed feasts of the LORD to himself and tells only the priests.

cards.text: So Moses announces the appointed feasts of the LORD to the Israelites, and the calendar is FULL. But God's not done teaching His people how to be holy, friend, so stick with me.

findings.problem: The card shortens the text's "vow offerings" to "the vows." In Leviticus 23:38 the listed items are all offerings that come in addition to the feast offerings. "The vows" names a different thing than the text does.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The right answer, "So their descendants know God made Israel dwell in booths," keeps the BSB words "descendants" and "dwell in booths." Both wrong answers are in plain modern wording, so the right answer sounds more like the Bible and stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
